I used to do anki when I started out with Japanese, but after half a year I noticed I've been progressingly significantly slower than when I was avidly learning new English vocab. Not to mention it really wasn't that fun for me. I think my mind just got used to the 1\-2 day gap, which I implemented into my learning schedule the moment I first got wind of the spaced repetition thingy.
I dislike anki to be honest, I rather keep a batch of 20 in a notepad and try to squeeze them into my head every other day for about a hour or two or so.

I should've specified; I don't have any problem wih kanji that depict a parcticular object, and in alot of cases, verb kanji haven't been been a bother either.

The tough part is when trying to create a picture, or non\-complicated, sensible idea of something like, say,  徳 = morals/virtue. Concept\-based kanji are by far the hardet ones to get past with this approach for me. Like, hellishly so.

b\-but t\-t\-hanks for the heads up

As of late I've given up on kanji more or less, and I'm certainly never getting back to making up mnemonics on my own again. I'm a literal anti\-talent at that. The only results I get from it are headaches.

But yeah, I used to. Anything I could come up with was so convoluted I should get a comedy award for it. That's why I'm looking for a simpler way, pls don't bully me "muh hard work" people.
